canonical_conversions.note: The canonical columns are unit conversions of the float32 values the original received and returned; no original formula is translated.

cost_guarded.note: The original produced a price for these rows from a NEGATIVE light basis because the load exceeds the displacement. This project refuses them: an impossible negative light basis is reported unavailable and never becomes a plausible zero price, even though the original emitted one.

limitations: Evidence only: no parity judgement, no replacement implementation, no ship validation, no whole-program or GUI parity claim.
Synthetic numerical inputs in imperial units; they are not user files and not ship data.

Original singleton-free instances only: no MainForm window is constructed, no designer InitializeComponent runs, no event handler is subscribed, no file of the installed application is opened for writing.
waterplaneArea_sqft of the synthetic ships is an input prepared from the standard Cwp = Aw/(L*B) relation; it is not produced by any method under test.
Unknown/null inputs are deliberately NOT probed here: the original fields are floats and cannot hold a null float, so the kernel unknown policy is outside this probe.

Deck selector, machinery and ammunition, forecastle and quarterdeck fractions, conning fore/aft and the year branch are swept; the paired cost readings isolate the three cost terms by zeroing one input at a time in the original costCalc, never by translating the formula.

original_binary.load_mode: Reflection.Assembly.LoadFile (read-only, in memory, no process launched)

original_convention.note: canonical m / mm / t values in this document are unit conversions of the float32 values the original assembly received and returned (ft*0.3048, in*25.4, LT*1.0160469088, sqft*0.092903); no original formula is translated in the harness

reading_convention.note: The probe isolates each cost term by differencing two complete costCalc readings at the same hull year, so its three term columns already carry the recovered year factor. This fixture stores them divided by that same factor, because the three contributions this project reports are the terms of the un-factored base. No original formula is translated and no original control wiring is reproduced.

scope: The original SpringSharpMono fixed armour weight methods and empirical cost methods executed directly on the recovered assembly, curated into a compact regression fixture. It is numerical evidence for the recovered expressions, nothing more: not whole-program parity, not GUI parity, not ship validation, and not a replacement implementation. No original code, control wiring or array initializer is reproduced here, only the inputs the original received and the numbers it returned.

armour.boundary_note: beltMainLength > hull.length makes the pow() base negative (non-integer exponent), so the original produces NaN, not a negative mass.
hull.length = 0 divides by zero inside the original; the result is a non-finite float, not an exception.
Cwp = 1.5 makes the exponent (1 - Cwp) negative.
Negative thickness input: the original multiplies it straight through and returns a negative mass.
Upper belt longer than the hull.
Selector 7 is outside the original 0..6 switch and falls into default, so only the fore/quarter terms survive.
Selector 9 is outside the original switch.
fc fraction 0 with Cwp > 1 evaluates pow(0, negative) = Infinity, which the original then multiplies by a zero factor.
Selector 4 (machinery box) with zero displacement divides by zero inside the original.
Negative deck thicknesses multiply straight through to a negative deck mass.
Zero displacement makes pow(0, 2/3) = 0: a known zero result, not an unknown, and not NaN.
